subject: math
title: Decimals: Tenths and Hundredths
seo_title: Grade 4 Decimals Worksheets: Tenths and Hundredths, Decimal Fractions, Number Lines and Comparing Decimals
standard_text: Express a fraction with denominator 10 as an equivalent fraction with denominator 100, and use this technique to add two fractions with respective denominators 10 and 100. Use decimal notation for fractions with denominators 10 or 100. Compare two decimals to hundredths by reasoning about their size, recognizing that comparisons are valid only when the two decimals refer to the same whole.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 decimals worksheets with hundredths grids: write tenths and hundredths as fractions and decimals, place decimals on a number line, add 3/10 + 45/100 and compare decimals like 0.5 and 0.45. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Tenths use one place after the point; hundredths use two. 7/10 = 0.7 and 7/100 = 0.07.
key_sub: 1 tenth = 10 hundredths, so 0.3 = 0.30. To compare or add, write both in hundredths: 0.5 = 0.50 is more than 0.45, and 3/10 + 45/100 = 30/100 + 45/100 = 75/100.
body_html:
Tenths and hundredths

Cut 1 whole into 10 equal parts: each part is one tenth, 110 = 0.1. Cut it into 100 equal parts: each part is one hundredth, 1100 = 0.01.

Tenths are hundredths too

Each tenth is 10 hundredths. Multiply the top and bottom by 10 to write tenths as hundredths.

Example

Add 310 + 45100.

Make the parts the same size first: 310 = 30100. Then 30100 + 45100 = 75100.

Answer: 75100 = 0.75

Place value after the point

NumberOnes.TenthsHundredthsFraction
0.470.4747100
0.070.077100
0.70.7710
2.052.052 and 5100

The first place after the point is tenths. The second place is hundredths. Use a 0 to hold a place: 7100 is 0.07, not 0.7.

Comparing decimals

Compare the ones, then the tenths, then the hundredths. Or write both numbers in hundredths.

Compare decimals only when they are parts of the same whole. 0.5 of a small pizza can be less than 0.4 of a large pizza.

Example

Which is greater: 0.8 or 0.75?

Write 0.8 as 0.80. 80 hundredths is more than 75 hundredths.

Answer: 0.8 is greater

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Writing 7100 as 0.7Hundredths use two places: 0.07
Thinking 0.45 > 0.5 because 45 > 5Compare tenths first, or write 0.5 as 0.50
Adding 310 + 45100 to get 48110Change tenths to hundredths, then add the tops only
Writing 710 as 7.10The bottom number is not written. 710 = 0.7
Comparing parts of different wholesCheck that both decimals name parts of the same whole

faq.q: How do you explain tenths and hundredths to 4th graders?
faq.a: Use one whole cut into 10 equal parts (tenths) and into 100 equal parts (hundredths). On a hundredths grid, one column is 1 tenth (0.1) and one small square is 1 hundredth (0.01).

faq.q: How do you write a fraction with a denominator of 10 or 100 as a decimal?
faq.a: Tenths use one place after the point and hundredths use two: 3/10 = 0.3 and 45/100 = 0.45. If the top number is less than 10, add a 0: 7/100 = 0.07.
First change the tenths to hundredths: 3/10 = 30/100. Then add the top numbers: 30/100 + 45/100 = 75/100, or 0.75.
0.5 is 5 tenths, which is 50 hundredths, and 0.45 is 45 hundredths. 50 hundredths is more, so 0.5 is bigger even though it has fewer digits.

sets.title: Read hundredths grids and tenths bars

items.q: What decimal names the shaded part of the grid?
items.e: The grid has 100 equal squares, so each square is 1 hundredth and each full column is 1 tenth. 4 full columns and 7 squares are shaded: 4 tenths and 7 hundredths. That is 47100 = 0.47.

items.q: What decimal names the shaded part of the grid?
items.e: The grid has 100 equal squares, so each square is 1 hundredth. Only 8 squares are shaded and there is no full column, so there are 0 tenths. 8 hundredths = 8100 = 0.08.

items.q: What decimal names the shaded part of the grid?

items.q: What decimal names the shaded part of the grid?

items.q: What fraction of the grid is shaded? Use hundredths.
items.e: Count the shaded squares: 30 squares out of 100 equal squares. The fraction is 30100. The bottom number is all 100 squares, not the white ones. (It is also 310, because 3 full columns are shaded.)

items.q: What fraction of the grid is shaded? Use hundredths.
items.e: Count the shaded squares: 24 squares out of 100 equal squares. The fraction is 24100. The bottom number is all 100 squares, not the white ones.

items.q: What fraction of the grid is shaded? Use hundredths.
items.e: Count the shaded squares: 9 squares out of 100 equal squares. The fraction is 9100. The bottom number is all 100 squares, not the white ones.

items.q: The whole bar is 1. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: The bar has 10 equal parts, so each part is 1 tenth. 7 parts are shaded: 710 = 0.7. One digit after the point means tenths.

items.q: The whole bar is 1. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: The bar has 10 equal parts, so each part is 1 tenth. 3 parts are shaded: 310 = 0.3. One digit after the point means tenths.

items.q: The whole bar is 1. What fraction is shaded?
items.e: The bar has 10 equal parts and 9 are shaded, so the shaded part is 910 (0.9).

items.q: The whole bar is 1. What fraction is shaded?
items.e: The bar has 10 equal parts and 4 are shaded, so the shaded part is 410 (0.4).

items.q: Each grid is 1 whole. What decimal names the shaded part?
items.e: Each grid is 1 whole. The first grid is all shaded: 1 whole. The second grid has 25 hundredths = 0.25. Together: 1 and 25 hundredths = 1.25.

items.q: Each grid is 1 whole. What decimal names the shaded part?
items.e: Each grid is 1 whole. The first grid is all shaded: 1 whole. The second grid has 6 hundredths = 0.06. Together: 1 and 6 hundredths = 1.06.

items.q: How many squares of a hundredths grid should you shade to show 0.4?
items.e: A hundredths grid has 100 squares, so you need the number of hundredths. 0.4 = 40100, so shade 40 squares. 4 tenths is the same as 40 hundredths: 4 full columns.

items.q: How many squares of a hundredths grid should you shade to show 0.35?
items.e: A hundredths grid has 100 squares, so you need the number of hundredths. 0.35 = 35100, so shade 35 squares.

items.q: How many squares of a hundredths grid should you shade to show 0.09?
items.e: A hundredths grid has 100 squares, so you need the number of hundredths. 0.09 = 9100, so shade 9 squares. The 0 in the tenths place means no full column.

items.q: How many squares of a hundredths grid should you shade to show 0.72?
items.e: A hundredths grid has 100 squares, so you need the number of hundredths. 0.72 = 72100, so shade 72 squares.

items.q: Write 7100 as a decimal.
items.e: 7100 means 7 hundredths. Hundredths need two digits after the point, so write a 0 in the tenths place: 0.07. (0.7 would be 7 tenths.)

items.q: Write 45100 as a decimal.
items.e: 45100 means 45 hundredths: 4 tenths and 5 hundredths. The hundredths digit goes in the second place after the point: 0.45.

items.q: Write 3100 as a decimal.
items.e: 3100 means 3 hundredths. Hundredths need two digits after the point, so write a 0 in the tenths place: 0.03. (0.3 would be 3 tenths.)

items.q: Write 80100 as a decimal.
items.e: 80100 = 0.8, because 80 hundredths is the same as 8 tenths. Both name the same point: 0.80 = 0.8.

items.q: Write 16100 as a decimal.
items.e: 16100 means 16 hundredths: 1 tenth and 6 hundredths. The hundredths digit goes in the second place after the point: 0.16.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.6?
items.e: 0.6 has one digit after the point, so it means 6 tenths: 610.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.09?
items.e: 0.09 has two digits after the point, so it means hundredths. 0.09 = 9 hundredths, which is 9100.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.32?
items.e: 0.32 has two digits after the point, so it means hundredths. 0.32 = 32 hundredths, which is 32100.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.05?
items.e: 0.05 has two digits after the point, so it means hundredths. 0.05 = 5 hundredths, which is 5100.

items.q: 310 = ?100
items.e: To go from tenths to hundredths, cut each tenth into 10 hundredths. Multiply the top and bottom by 10: 310 = 30100. The bottom number grew by ×10, so the top number must too.

items.q: 710 = ?100
items.e: To go from tenths to hundredths, cut each tenth into 10 hundredths. Multiply the top and bottom by 10: 710 = 70100. The bottom number grew by ×10, so the top number must too.

items.q: 510 = ?100
items.e: To go from tenths to hundredths, cut each tenth into 10 hundredths. Multiply the top and bottom by 10: 510 = 50100. The bottom number grew by ×10, so the top number must too.

items.q: Which decimal is equal to 0.7?
items.e: 0.7 is 7 tenths. 7 tenths = 70 hundredths, so 0.7 = 0.70. A 0 at the end does not change the value. A 0 right after the point does: 0.07 is only 7 hundredths.

items.q: What is the value of the 8 in 0.58?
items.e: The 8 is the second digit after the point, the hundredths place. Its value is 8 hundredths (0.08).

items.q: What is the value of the 6 in 4.63?
items.e: The 6 is the first digit after the point, the tenths place. Its value is 6 tenths (0.6). Tens are on the left of the ones; tenths are on the right of the point.

items.q: Which digit is in the hundredths place in 17.35?
items.e: Places after the point: tenths first (3), then hundredths (5). The 1 is in the tens place, not the hundreds place.

items.q: Which digit is in the tenths place in 52.86?
items.e: The tenths place is the first digit after the point: 8. The 5 is in the tens place, on the other side of the point.

items.q: Which decimal is thirty-six hundredths?
items.e: Hundredths means two digits after the point: 36 hundredths = 36100 = 0.36.

items.q: Which decimal is two and five tenths?
items.e: “And” marks the decimal point. 2 wholes and 5 tenths: 2.5. (2.05 would be 5 hundredths.)

items.q: Which decimal is four and seven hundredths?
items.e: 4 wholes, then the point. 7 hundredths needs two places, so put a 0 in the tenths place: 4.07.

items.q: What decimal is at the red dot?
items.e: From 0 to 1 there are 10 equal spaces, so each space is 1 tenth (0.1). The dot is 7 spaces from 0: 710 = 0.7. Count spaces, not tick marks.

items.e: The line starts at 1, not 0. Each space is 1 tenth. The dot is 9 spaces past 1: 1 and 9 tenths = 1.9.

items.q: What decimal is at the red dot?
items.e: This line goes from 0.3 to 0.4, which is 1 tenth. It is cut into 10 equal spaces, so each space is 1 hundredth. 0.3 = 0.30. The dot is 6 spaces past 0.30: 0.36.

items.q: What decimal is at the red dot?
items.e: This line goes from 0.7 to 0.8, which is 1 tenth. It is cut into 10 equal spaces, so each space is 1 hundredth. 0.7 = 0.70. The dot is 2 spaces past 0.70: 0.72.

items.q: What decimal is at the red dot?
items.e: This line goes from 0.1 to 0.2, which is 1 tenth. It is cut into 10 equal spaces, so each space is 1 hundredth. 0.1 = 0.10. The dot is 8 spaces past 0.10: 0.18.

items.q: What decimal is at the red dot?
items.e: This line goes from 0.5 to 0.6, which is 1 tenth. It is cut into 10 equal spaces, so each space is 1 hundredth. 0.5 = 0.50. The dot is 5 spaces past 0.50: 0.55.

items.q: Which point is at 0.3?
items.e: Each space is 1 tenth. 0.3 is 3 tenths, so count 3 spaces from 0. That is point B.

items.q: Which point is at 0.6?
items.e: Each space is 1 tenth. 0.6 is 6 tenths, so count 6 spaces from 0. That is point C.

items.q: Which point is at 1.8?

items.q: Which point is at 0.8?
items.e: Each space is 1 tenth. 0.8 is 8 tenths, so count 8 spaces from 0. That is point A.

sets.title: Add tenths and hundredths, compare decimals

items.q: 310 + 45100 = ?
items.e: You can only add parts of the same size. Change tenths to hundredths: 310 = 30100. Then add: 30100 + 45100 = 75100. Never add the bottom numbers.

items.q: 210 + 6100 = ?
items.e: You can only add parts of the same size. Change tenths to hundredths: 210 = 20100. Then add: 20100 + 6100 = 26100. Never add the bottom numbers.

items.q: 510 + 31100 = ?
items.e: You can only add parts of the same size. Change tenths to hundredths: 510 = 50100. Then add: 50100 + 31100 = 81100. Never add the bottom numbers.

items.q: 610 + 18100 = ?
items.e: You can only add parts of the same size. Change tenths to hundredths: 610 = 60100. Then add: 60100 + 18100 = 78100. Never add the bottom numbers.

items.q: 410 + 9100 = ?
items.e: You can only add parts of the same size. Change tenths to hundredths: 410 = 40100. Then add: 40100 + 9100 = 49100. Never add the bottom numbers.

items.q:
Add. Write the sum as a decimal.
410 + 25100 = ?
items.e: 410 = 40100, so 40100 + 25100 = 65100 = 0.65.

items.q:
Add. Write the sum as a decimal.
710 + 45100 = ?
items.e: 710 = 70100, so 70100 + 45100 = 115100 = 1.15. That is more than 1 whole, because 100 hundredths make 1.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: Write 0.5 with hundredths: 0.5 = 0.50. Now compare 50 hundredths and 45 hundredths: 0.5 > 0.45. A longer number is not always bigger: compare the tenths first.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: Write 0.3 with hundredths: 0.3 = 0.30. Now compare 30 hundredths and 28 hundredths: 0.3 > 0.28. A longer number is not always bigger: compare the tenths first.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: Write 0.7 with hundredths: 0.7 = 0.70. Now compare 7 hundredths and 70 hundredths: 0.07 < 0.7. 0.07 has 0 tenths; 0.7 has 7 tenths.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: Write 0.9 with hundredths: 0.9 = 0.90. Now compare 90 hundredths and 89 hundredths: 0.9 > 0.89. A longer number is not always bigger: compare the tenths first.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: Write 0.4 with hundredths: 0.4 = 0.40. Now compare 42 hundredths and 40 hundredths: 0.42 > 0.4.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: Compare the ones first: 1.3 has 1 whole and 0.95 has 0 wholes, so 1.3 > 0.95.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: Write 0.3 with hundredths: 0.3 = 0.30. Now compare 25 hundredths and 30 hundredths: 0.25 < 0.3.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: 0.6 is 6 tenths, and 6 tenths = 60 hundredths = 0.60. A 0 at the end does not change the value, so they are equal.

items.q: Grid A shows 0.5. Grid B shows 0.45. Which is true?
items.e: Count squares: A has 50 shaded and B has 45. More of grid A is shaded, so 0.5 > 0.45, even though 45 is bigger than 5.

items.q: Which decimal is the greatest?
items.e: Compare the tenths first: 0.6 has 6 tenths, while 0.45, 0.38 and 0.09 have 4, 3 and 0 tenths. 0.6 is the greatest, even though it has fewer digits.

items.q: Which decimal is the smallest?
items.e: Compare the tenths first: 0.05 has 0 tenths, while 0.5, 0.15 and 0.51 have 5, 1 and 5 tenths. So 0.05 is the smallest.

items.q: Order from least to greatest.
items.e: Write them all as hundredths: 0.09 = 9, 0.4 = 40, 0.62 = 62 hundredths. 9 < 40 < 62, so the order is 0.09, 0.4, 0.62.

items.q: Order from greatest to least.
items.e: 1.2 has a whole, so it is the greatest. Then 0.8 = 0.80 is more than 0.75. The order is 1.2, 0.8, 0.75.

items.q: A dime is 110 of a dollar and a penny is 1100 of a dollar. Ava has 3 dimes and 4 pennies. How much money does she have?
items.e: 3 dimes = 310, 4 pennies = 4100. In all: 34100 of a dollar = $0.34. Count the value, not the number of coins.

items.q: A dime is 110 of a dollar and a penny is 1100 of a dollar. Lily has 5 dimes. How much money does she have?
items.e: 5 dimes = 510 = 50100 of a dollar = $0.50. 5 tenths = 50 hundredths, which is 50 cents.

items.q: A dime is 110 of a dollar and a penny is 1100 of a dollar. Grace has 1 dime and 8 pennies. How much money does she have?
items.e: 1 dime = 110, 8 pennies = 8100. In all: 18100 of a dollar = $0.18. Count the value, not the number of coins.

items.q: Zoe wants to pay $0.85 with only dimes and pennies, using the fewest coins. Which coins does she use?
items.e: $0.85 = 8 tenths and 5 hundredths. A dime is a tenth and a penny is a hundredth: 8 dimes and 5 pennies. 85 pennies is also $0.85, but it uses many more coins.

items.q: Luis has 4 dimes. He finds 25 pennies. How much money does he have now?
items.e: 4 dimes = 410 = 40100. Add the pennies: 40100 + 25100 = 65100 = $0.65. Do not add 4 and 25: a dime is worth 10 pennies.

items.q: Noah has 6 dimes. Owen has 5 dimes and 8 pennies. Who has more money?
items.e: Noah has $0.60. Owen has $0.58. 60 cents is more than 58 cents, so Noah has more, even though Owen has more coins.

items.q: How many pennies make 0.3 of a dollar?
items.e: 0.3 = 310 = 30100. A penny is 1 hundredth of a dollar, so you need 30 pennies (30 cents).

items.q: A plant grew 0.3 meter in spring and 0.25 meter in summer. How much did it grow in all?
items.e: 0.3 = 30100. Add hundredths to hundredths: 30100 + 25100 = 55100 = 0.55 m. Line up the tenths with the tenths.

items.q: Leo jumped 1.4 meters. Omar jumped 1.35 meters. Who jumped farther?
items.e: Both jumped 1 whole meter. Compare the tenths: 1.4 has 4 tenths, 1.35 has 3 tenths. 1.4 = 1.40 > 1.35, so Leo jumped farther. More digits does not mean bigger.

items.q: Three pencils are 0.15 m, 0.2 m and 0.12 m long. Which pencil is the shortest?
items.e: Write all as hundredths: 0.15 = 15, 0.2 = 20, 0.12 = 12 hundredths. The shortest is 0.12 m. 0.2 is not the shortest: 2 tenths is 20 hundredths.

items.q: Jack ate 0.5 of a small pizza. Mia ate 0.4 of a large pizza. Jack says he ate more because 0.5 > 0.4. Is he right?
items.e: You can compare decimals only when they are parts of the same whole. Half of a small pizza can be less than 0.4 of a large pizza, so Jack cannot be sure.

items.q: Two water bottles are the same size. One is 0.8 full. The other is 0.75 full. Which has more water?
items.e: The bottles are the same size, so you can compare. 0.8 = 0.80, and 80 hundredths > 75 hundredths. The 0.8 bottle has more.

items.q: A garden has 100 equal plots. Tomatoes grow in 23 of them. What decimal names the part with tomatoes?
items.e: 23 out of 100 equal plots is 23100 = 0.23.

items.q: A class has 10 students. 7 of them walk to school. What decimal names the part of the class that walks?
items.e: 7 out of 10 students is 710. Tenths have one digit after the point: 0.7. (0.3 is the part that does not walk.)

items.q: A recipe needs 0.5 liter of milk and 0.25 liter of cream. How much is that in all?
items.e: 0.5 = 510 = 50100. Then 50100 + 25100 = 75100 = 0.75 L. Add tenths to tenths and hundredths to hundredths.

items.q: A meter has 100 centimeters. A crayon is 9 centimeters long. How long is it in meters?
items.e: Each centimeter is 1100 of a meter. 9 centimeters = 9100 = 0.09 m. (0.9 m would be 90 centimeters.)

items.q: Kai says 0.3 = 0.30. Is he right?
items.e: 0.3 is 3 tenths. 3 tenths = 30 hundredths = 0.30. A 0 at the end does not change the value, so Kai is right.

items.q: A board 1 meter long is cut into 10 equal pieces. Nora uses 4 pieces. How many meters of board does she use?
items.e: Each piece is 110 of a meter. 4 pieces = 410 = 0.4 m.

items.q: A trail has a sign every tenth of a mile. Emma walks past the 1-mile sign and then 3 more signs. How far has she walked?
items.e: 1 mile, then 3 tenths more: 1 + 0.3 = 1.3 miles. Each sign is 0.1 mile, not 0.01.

items.q: A rope is 0.6 meter long. Sofia adds a piece that is 0.08 meter long. How long is the rope now?
items.e: 0.6 = 60100. Then 60100 + 8100 = 68100 = 0.68 m. The 8 is hundredths, so it goes in the second place.
